newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures end down in flat trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures end down in flat trade.

text.p: Rubber futures closed lower on Monday after players liquidated their positions while flat prices in Japan depressed market sentiment, dealers said.

"There were some European houses closing their positions by liquidating their holdings, but the volume was noticeably thin. It's really been very quiet for most of the day," a local rubber dealer said.

Most of the buying was focused on RSS3 and RSS1 rubber. The most active months were the May RSS3 contract with some 600 tonnes traded and the October/December RSS1 contract with some 900 tonnes traded, dealers said.
"Japan was also steady to flat and that was something of a dampener for business today," another dealer said.
Tokyo's benchmark July contract closed unchanged at 156.0 yen. In Kobe, the key July contract slipped 0.5 yen to 155.3.
At around 0945 GMT, April RSS3 was seen at 122.00-123.00 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 123.00 cents.
October/December RSS1 was seen at 177.00-179.00 Singapore cents (US$1.25-$1.27) a kg from the previous 179.00 cents.
April TSR20 was seen at 168.00-170.00 Singapore cents (US$1.19-$1.20) a kg against 169.75 cents.
